gap: Scoping is clean (BHD control is pixel-identical to baseline, AE=0), so this is a pure design loss. Ours tells the user something false and then hides it. With an impossible filter on /invoice (37 invoices exist, 0 matched) the panel reads 'No Data Found / Records you add will be listed here.' — a first-run zero-state message shown for a no-search-results condition — and offers no Clear search / Clear filters affordance, so the block is a dead end whose only nearby CTA (Add New Invoice) is the wrong action. On desktop that wrong message sits alone in a ~460px void behind a 60px icon. At 390x844 it is worse: the empty block starts at y=704 and its message occupies 820-872 CSS px, i.e. behind the fixed bottom tab bar (top ~790) and past the 844px fold, so the entire empty state is unreadable without scrolling a 1089px document. The nicer icon tile and 17px/600 title are a real gain over stock AntD's 14px grey tray, but a state that lies about the account and then falls off the phone does not read as calmer, more competent or more expensive than the bar's dense, truthful, shipped transactions screen.
